question: From the top of a hill 240 metres high, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a pole are 30Â° and 60Â°, respectively. The difference (in metres) between the height of the pole and its distance from the hill is:
solution:
**Given:**

Height of hill = 240 m

Angle of depression to top of pole = 30°

Angle of depression to bottom of pole = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tanθ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/476b28939adf91a524151e5a2c69d449bb8d6da92809c01a7c95abda8cbf8fb5.png] 

⇒ tan60° = 240 ÷ Distance

⇒ √3 = 240 ÷ Distance

⇒ Distance = 240 ÷ √3

⇒ Distance = 80√3

⇒ tan30° = (240 − Height of pole) ÷ Distance

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = (240 − Height) ÷ 80√3

⇒ 240 − Height = 80

⇒ Height = 160

⇒ Difference = 160 − 80√3

⇒ = 80(2 − √3)

**∴ The correct answer is 80(2 − √3).**
